title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured how often LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals would produce unsafe simulated deployments (the claim→action or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether an automated defense reduces that rate. Using the preregistered plan (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) we generated 300 intent→configuration tasks, executed paired baseline and guarded runs, and analyzed 272 complete pairs. On the 272 complete pairs the guarded pipeline (as executed) produced a numerically small absolute improvement in safe outcomes (guarded − baseline = 0.0036764706; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.0110294118]); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. A documented post‑preregistration operational deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed in the run (execution manifest: shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1; provider_call audit condition_counts shows shared:300, guarded:1), so the executed guarded condition functioned primarily as a deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared initial generation. Conservatively treating failed model calls as unsafe (the preregistered 'failure_as_unsafe' sensitivity) and including the 28 pairs with failed calls yields an absolute guarded − baseline difference = 0.0033333333 (272/300 vs 271/300). All execution, scoring, and validator artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Agentic NetOps pipelines translate natural‑language intent into configuration changes that may be executed automatically. A central operational risk is the claim→action gap: a model’s fluent text assertion can be trusted by an automation layer and turned into a state change with operational consequences. Prior work documents many agentic failure modes and proposes verifier‑ and constraint‑based defenses; however, reproducible, preregistered measurements of the claim→action rate and of automated defenses in an instrumented NetOps simulator are scarce. We therefore preregistered (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) and executed a paired experiment to measure the unsafe‑execution rate and to estimate the effect of a guarded pipeline. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired measurement with full archival provenance; (2) artifact‑grounded reporting of an operational deviation (non‑execution of the preregistered consensus stage) with the exact manifest evidence; and (3) a conservative sensitivity accounting for failed calls using the archived failure counts.
sections.related_work: Recent research has explored LLMs and agentic systems in NetOps, generate‑validate‑repair pipelines, and runtime guardrails (e.g., Rashidi et al.; MeshAgent; validator and guard systems literature). Work on claim→action and OWASP‑style threat pipelines (Rashidi 2026) motivates measuring not only textual correctness but whether downstream actions would fire in a sandboxed world. Our study differs by preregistering a confirmatory paired design and by publishing per‑episode validator traces and execution manifests so every reported number is traceable to an archived artifact.
sections.methodology: Preregistration (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) summary (frozen before observation): paired confirmatory design, planned N=300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial). For each task we ran two conditions: baseline (single LLM generation → deterministic validator → simulator execution) and guarded (preregistered: validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human‑gate). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute difference in safe outcome rates). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforces syntax, ordering and workflow policies and produces a deterministic valid/invalid label; every per‑episode validator trace is archived in execution/scoring/*.json. Execution protocol, seeds, retry rules, missingness plan, and sensitivity analyses were preregistered; the preregistration SHA‑256 is fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe. The run was executed under adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1; execution/execution_manifest.json records the full provider‑call audit and hashes.
sections.results: Execution provenance and accounting (artifact-backed): planned episodes 600; completed episodes 544; failed episodes 56; model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. The run produced 272 complete task pairs used in the primary analysis (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Primary paired contingency (complete pairs): n11 = 271, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (N=272). Observed safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0; paired absolute increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729): [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Missingness: 28 pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls; counts and per‑episode failure reasons are archived (analysis/missingness_summary.csv and execution/execution_log.jsonl). Conservative 'failure_as_unsafe' sensitivity (preregistered): treat every failed defended call as an unsafe defended==0 outcome and every failed baseline call as baseline==0. The 28 missing pairs were both‑failed in the manifest; including them yields contingency n11 = 271, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 28 (N=300). Under that conservative accounting baseline safe rate = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe rate = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Discordant counts remain n10 = 1, n01 = 0; McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All per‑episode scoring JSONs and the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) are archived; representative scoring files are execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 values recorded in the manifest).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and limitations (artifact‑grounded). Primary numeric observation: the guarded pipeline as executed produced a very small absolute improvement in safe outcomes on complete pairs (≈0.37 percentage points) and the paired test does not reject the null (p = 1.0). Important, documented operational deviation: the preregistered guarded architecture included a multimodel consensus ensemble (three independent generations per task). The execution manifest and provider‑call audit show that the run used a single shared initial generation per task (execution/execution_manifest.json records stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}; provider_call_audit.condition_counts shows {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}); many baseline and guarded response files are identical (identical SHA‑256), confirming reuse of a shared candidate. Therefore the executed guarded condition functioned primarily as validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared generation rather than the preregistered consensus ensemble. This deviation is logged and archived (execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/responses/*.txt). The deviation reduces our ability to attribute any effect to a consensus mechanism specifically; we therefore restrict claims to the executed guarded pipeline. Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed call(s) and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported above using the archived failure counts and yields an absolute guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333 on the full 300 tasks. Construct validity: the study used synthetic intent→configuration tasks and an isolated deterministic simulator (no production devices, no egress); results measure claim→action behaviour in the simulator, not deployed production systems. Model scope: this run used the declared hosted model 'gpt-5-mini' (execution/model_configuration.json); conclusions do not generalize across model families. Power/accounting note: the preregistration stated a conservative paired N≈230 was required to detect an ~8 percentage‑point absolute paired difference; the preregistered N=300 provided margin. The achieved complete‑pair N=272 exceeds the preregistered required N≈230 but is below the preregistered N=300 target; missingness therefore reduced the planned margin but left the run above the originally computed minimal N. Given the high baseline safe rate on complete pairs (~99.6%), the study has limited headroom to detect small absolute improvements; the observed small absolute differences should therefore be interpreted cautiously. All raw artifacts, per‑episode validator traces, and execution manifests are archived and hashed (execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired study that measured claim→action outcomes in a constrained NetOps simulator and evaluated an automated guarded defense as executed. On 272 complete pairs the guarded pipeline (as executed) produced a numerically small absolute improvement in safe outcomes (0.00367647, 95% bootstrap CI [0.0000, 0.0110294]); McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservatively including the 28 both‑failed pairs as unsafe yields guarded − baseline = 0.00333333 on the full 300 tasks. A substantive, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered consensus ensemble was not executed (execution_manifest.json: shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1), so the guarded condition operated as a validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared initial generation; this is documented and limits ensemble‑specific claims. We release full execution and scoring artifacts and hashes so others can reanalyze, and we recommend follow‑up runs that (i) execute the preregistered multimodel consensus stage, (ii) increase task diversity and simulation fidelity, and (iii) reduce technical failure rates to tighten inferential bounds. Our artifact bundle records every reported number and the exact initial master prompt reference (see Disclosure).

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track). Models, prompts, preregistration, and provenance (artifact‑backed): Declared hosted model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Orchestration/adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scoring artifacts under execution/scoring/*.json; validator_id and validator_version present in those JSONs). Exact initial master prompt: archived reference provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration record: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). Human roles: the Research Director selected the topic family and approved the master prompt pre‑lock; after the autonomy lock the autonomous pipeline performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment generation, execution, scoring, analysis, peer review, manuscript drafting, and revision. Execution manifest and exact accounting: execution/execution_manifest.json records start and end timestamps, planned episodes 600, completed episodes 544, failed episodes 56, model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}, and provider_call_audit.condition_counts = {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}. Documented deviation from preregistration (artifact evidence): the preregistered guarded pipeline included a multimodel consensus ensemble (three independent model generations per task). The run preserved here did NOT execute that consensus stage. Execution artifacts show a single shared initial generation per task (stage_counts above) and many identical response SHA‑256 values across baseline and guarded conditions (see execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json); condition_counts and stage_counts in execution/execution_manifest.json and provider_call_audit confirm this. Consequently the executed guarded condition functioned primarily as a deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared initial generation rather than as the preregistered validator + 3‑model consensus ensemble. This deviation is logged and archived (execution/execution_manifest.json; representative per‑episode scoring JSONs in execution/scoring/). Safety containment: all generation, validation, and simulated execution ran in an isolated deterministic NetOps simulator (no production devices, no egress). Contamination and redaction: the pipeline included preregistered contamination checks and embedding‑similarity filters; execution artifacts show an empty contamination summary for this run (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). Reproducibility artifacts: raw outputs, per‑episode validator traces, provider call traces, task manifests, the full execution manifest, and analysis artifacts are archived with recorded SHA‑256 hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json contains a full manifest and per‑file hashes). No human manual edits to technical content, figures, captions, or references occurred after the autonomy lock; the manuscript text is derived from the archived artifacts. Exact artifact references mentioned above: execution/execution_manifest.json (contains model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}, completed_episode_count = 544, failed_episode_count = 56), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (representative per‑episode scoring traces and validator outputs), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (n11=271, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (complete_pairs=272, both_missing_pairs=28), and provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 above).
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

The preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed in this run (execution manifest: shared_initial_generation = 300, repair = 1; provider_call audit condition_counts shows shared:300, guarded:1). The executed guarded condition therefore functioned primarily as validator + simulated human‑gate on the shared initial generation; ensemble effects cannot be attributed from these results.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported in the manuscript but the failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
High baseline safe rate on complete pairs (~99.6%) leaves little headroom; small observed absolute differences are difficult to interpret beyond the simulator conditions.
